surface: nix/generators/base.nix:21 (services.gapi.agentsDir); nix/module.nix:52-67 (the agentsDir option's own documentation), :212 (GAPI_AGENT_PATH), :228 (/etc/gapi/agents tmpfiles), :229-230 (the agentsDir tmpfiles rule); nix/generators/base.nix:69-90 (environment.etc, where the shipped agents actually go)
violation: THE GENERATOR CONTRADICTS THE MODULE IT IMPORTS, AND CONTRADICTS OPERATOR DECISION 9. nix/generators/base.nix:21 sets services.gapi.agentsDir = "/var/lib/gapi/agents". The option it is setting documents the opposite in the text an operator reads (nix/module.nix:60-62): '/var/lib/gapi is state (the database, certificates) and is deliberately NOT an agent directory: agents are executable payload, not variable state.' Operator decision 9 reserves /var/lib for STATE ONLY. base.nix imports ../module.nix at :16, so the file setting the value is the file that ships the documentation forbidding it. IT IS THE EXACT VALUE GAPI-DIV-063 WAS FILED TO REMOVE. That entry records: 'This used to default to /var/lib/gapi/agents and was passed as GAPI_AGENT_PATH, which REPLACED the whole search path - so every tier below it was dead on a packaged install (GAPI-DIV-063).' The module was fixed and the generator kept the old spelling. Moving a fix does not move its literals. WHAT THIS ACTUALLY DID ON A BUILT IMAGE, and it is worse than a style violation. The two agents every generator image ships - heartbeat.py.timer and sysinfo.py.service - are installed through environment.etc at base.nix:69-90, which places them in /etc/gapi/agents. The image therefore creates an EMPTY /var/lib/gapi/agents (module.nix:229-230 makes it 0750 under the service user whenever agentsDir is non-null), points GAPI_AGENT_PATH at that empty directory (:212), and leaves its only real agents in a different tier. UNDER THE PRE-063 REPLACING BEHAVIOUR THAT MADE BOTH SHIPPED AGENTS UNDISCOVERABLE - every advertised image booted with an agent directory it could not search. The additive fix silently repaired that and left the cause in place, so the defect is currently INERT: an extra empty path on the search list costs nothing. NOT CLAIMED AS A LIVE FAILURE TODAY. What is claimed is that a documented policy is violated by the repository's own images, and that the inertness depends entirely on a behaviour GAPI-DIV-063 is still open about.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (documentation describes what exists; a module whose own option text forbids the value its generator sets is wrong in one place or the other); operator decision 9 (/usr/lib for packages, /etc for operators, /var/lib for STATE ONLY)
exit: DELETE THE agentsDir LINE FROM nix/generators/base.nix, which is the whole fix and is one line. agentsDir defaults to null; with it unset the image searches the built-in tiers, /etc/gapi/agents among them, which is where the image's own agents already are. The option exists for agents living somewhere non-standard, and nothing in these images does. CLOSES ON: the line removed, plus an assertion that the shipped agents are actually FOUND rather than merely present - nix/tests/module-boot.nix:82 today asserts 'test -d /etc/gapi/agents', which proves the directory exists and says nothing about whether gapid searched it. That distinction is the entire subject of this entry and of GAPI-DIV-063, so an exit that only checks the directory would repeat the mistake. The discriminating assertion is that gapid reports heartbeat and sysinfo as discovered agents on a booted image. NOT AN EXIT: setting agentsDir to /etc/gapi/agents instead, which makes the option redundant with a built-in tier and re-teaches the habit of naming a search path explicitly; or creating the agents under /var/lib to match the setting, which violates decision 9 in the other direction. SEQUENCING: this is independent of GAPI-DIV-063 and does not wait on it, but the two share a subject and the honest reading is that 063's fix was never carried to the generators. Anyone closing 063 should check base.nix first. RESIDUAL ON ARRIVAL: no gate compares a generator's settings against the policy its imported module documents, so the next such contradiction is found the same way this one was - by reading. ||| RESOLVED 2026-08-04. THE ONE-LINE FIX WAS THE ONE LINE THIS ENTRY SAID IT WAS, and the exit's insistence on a discovery assertion rather than a directory check is what earned its keep: writing that assertion uncovered THREE further defects, each of which alone would have kept the shipped agents unusable, and none of which any directory check could see. nix/generators/base.nix no longer sets agentsDir. VERIFIED against the evaluated configuration first (agentsDir null, no GAPI_AGENT_PATH on the unit) and then on a booted guest, which now logs 'scanning agent search path path=/etc/gapi/agents path_type=SYSTEM' - the tier this entry was filed about is searched. CLOSED ON nix/tests/generator-agents.nix, registered in nix/checks.nix, which boots ../generators/base.nix rather than the module (the defect was in the generator; testing the module would have passed throughout) and asserts: both agent files present, NO GAPI_AGENT_PATH on the unit, NO /var/lib/gapi/agents, gapi.service ACTIVE, and gapictl agent status naming BOTH heartbeat and sysinfo. WHAT THE DISCOVERY ASSERTION FOUND, in the order it found them: (1) gapi.service could not start on any image at all, dying on a certificate the module named and nothing created - GAPI-DIV-076. (2) With the daemon up and the directory searched, discovery still reported count=0: no image carried the Python ADK runner or an interpreter, and resolvePyRunner's last resort is a cwd-relative path that only ever resolves in a developer checkout - GAPI-DIV-077. (3) With the runner shipped, count=1 under the id 'unknown': neither shipped agent declared an ID, so they collided and one was dropped - GAPI-DIV-078. (4) Underneath all three, discovery swallows describe failures with no log line, which is why each of these presented as a silent zero - GAPI-DIV-079, filed OPEN. THE ENTRY'S OWN WARNING WAS CORRECT AND UNDERSTATED. It said an exit that only checked the directory 'would repeat the mistake'. In fact a directory check would have passed at every one of the four stages above, including the one where the daemon was in a permanent restart loop. RESIDUAL ON ARRIVAL, now discharged: 'no gate compares a generator's settings against the policy its imported module documents'. Still true as a general statement - generator-agents.nix asserts this specific consequence, not the general policy - so the next such contradiction is still found by reading.

surface: nix/module.nix:88-98 (certFile/keyFile, formerly types.path with /var/lib/gapi/certs defaults), :24-39 (the emitted config), :223 (the tmpfiles rule that creates the DIRECTORY); core/transport/factory.go:33-47 (the self-signed fallback the defaults made unreachable); nix/tests/module-boot.nix:20 (the hedge that hid it)
violation: EVERY ADVERTISED IMAGE SHIPPED A gapi.service THAT COULD NOT START. certFile and keyFile were types.path defaulting to /var/lib/gapi/certs/server.crt and .key, and the module wrote both into the generated config unconditionally. systemd.tmpfiles created the DIRECTORY (:223); nothing ever created the FILES. So the daemon read a config naming a certificate, took transport/factory.go's 'a cert is configured' branch at :42, and died: 'supervisor init: transport init: load cert: open /var/lib/gapi/certs/server.crt: no such file or directory', then restarted, forever. NAMING A PATH IS NOT PROVISIONING ONE, and the module could not tell its own guess from an operator's instruction. THE WORKING FALLBACK WAS UNREACHABLE PRECISELY BECAUSE THE MODULE ALWAYS FILLED THE OPTION: factory.go:33 falls back to a generated self-signed certificate when tlsCert or tlsKey is empty, warning loudly that it is not for production. On a NixOS image that branch could never run. FOUND BY THE GAPI-DIV-075 TEST, not by inspection, and it had been invisible to the existing gate for a reason worth recording: nix/tests/module-boot.nix:20 states it 'deliberately does NOT assert that gapid reaches an active state under every configuration: that depends on runtime setup this test does not supply'. That hedge is reasonable in isolation and it was covering a daemon in a permanent restart loop. A test that declines to check the thing MOST likely to be broken reads as caution and functions as a blindfold.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 5 (a mechanism that cannot run in the configuration that ships is not a mechanism); operator decision 2 (no usable default for identity - which cuts BOTH ways: an image must not ship a credential, and must not require one that nothing provides)
exit: RESOLVED 2026-08-04. certFile and keyFile are now nullOr types.path defaulting to null, matching agentsDir and verifyKey in the same file - the module's own established shape for 'the operator may supply this'. tlsCert/tlsKey are emitted only when BOTH are non-null, so a stock image carries no TLS keys in its config and the daemon's own self-signed fallback runs and warns. An operator who sets them gets exactly what they named. /var/lib/gapi/certs is still created, because it is where a provisioned certificate goes. CLOSES ON nix/tests/generator-agents.nix, which waits for gapi.service and then requires gapictl to answer - a daemon in a restart loop fails both. VERIFIED: the guest journal now carries 'no TLS cert/key configured; using auto-generated self-signed certificate (insecure, not for production)' followed by 'quic listener started' and 'supervisor running', where it previously carried the load-cert error and a Usage dump. module-boot.nix was UPDATED RATHER THAN WEAKENED: its assertions that the config says tlsCert and not certFile are about the viper mapstructure spelling (GAPI-DIV-033), a question that only exists when a certificate is configured, so its node now configures one and both assertions still run. RESIDUAL: a self-signed certificate is the honest default for an image that also ships no credential, but it is not a production posture, and nothing tells an operator they are running on one except a WARN line in the journal. The image documentation does not mention certificates at all.

surface: nix/package.nix (postInstall, formerly absent; python3 was a buildInput only); core/supervisor/lifecycle_handlers.go:200-213 (resolvePyRunner and its cwd-relative last resort); core/agentmgr/discovery.go:215-223 (the python branch) and :466-490 (pythonDescribe, which needs both the runner and an interpreter)
violation: THE PYTHON ADK IS PART OF THE PRODUCT AND WAS PACKAGED AS IF IT WERE A DEVELOPMENT CONVENIENCE. A Python agent is described by executing adk/python/agent/runner.py against it, so a gapid with no runner cannot discover a *.py.service, *.py.timer or *.py.socket AT ALL. nix/package.nix installed two Go binaries and nothing else: no runner, and python3 only as a buildInput, which does not put an interpreter on the running daemon's PATH. resolvePyRunner looks in three places - GAPI_PY_RUNNER, then adk/python/agent/runner.py NEXT TO THE BINARY, then THE SAME PATH RELATIVE TO THE CURRENT DIRECTORY. THE LAST ONE IS WHY THIS SURVIVED SO LONG: in a developer checkout the cwd fallback happens to hit, so every local run worked; a systemd unit runs with cwd at /, where it cannot. The defect was therefore invisible in exactly the environment it was developed in and fatal in the one that ships - the same shape as GAPI-DIV-063's fence, inverted. MEASURED on a booted image: 'agent discovery complete count=0' with both shipped agents present in the searched directory.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 5 (a language SDK is part of the product surface, not a development aid); go-project-manifesto (a binary's runtime dependencies belong in its package, not in the ambient environment of whoever built it)
exit: RESOLVED 2026-08-04. nix/package.nix gained a postInstall that copies adk/python into $out/share/gapi/python and wraps gapid with GAPI_PY_RUNNER pointing at it plus python3 on PATH. FIXED IN THE PACKAGE RATHER THAN IN module.nix ON PURPOSE, so every consumer of the derivation gets a working runner and not only NixOS - the module is one consumer of the package, and a runtime dependency satisfied only by one consumer is not satisfied. The wrapper sets the override EXPLICITLY instead of relying on the next-to-the-binary probe: $out/bin holds binaries, and burying a python tree there to satisfy a path probe is the sort of layout a later tidy-up deletes without knowing it was load-bearing. gapictl is deliberately NOT wrapped - it does not discover agents, and a python on its PATH that it never calls is scope the wrapper cannot justify. --set-default rather than --set, so an operator's GAPI_PY_RUNNER still wins. CLOSES ON nix/tests/generator-agents.nix asserting gapid reports the shipped agents as discovered. VERIFIED: the guest journal went from 'agent discovery complete count=0' to two 'registered agent' lines and 'count=2'. RESIDUAL 1, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS TOOK FOUR ITERATIONS TO FIND: core/agentmgr/discovery.go:220 SWALLOWS the describe error - the comment reads 'quiet for mixed folders' - so a file that matched the agent naming convention and then failed to describe is discarded with no log line at any level. That turned a missing interpreter into a silent count of zero. Filed separately as GAPI-DIV-079 and NOT fixed here. RESIDUAL 2: resolvePyRunner's cwd-relative last resort is still there and is still a trap of the same shape for any non-Nix deployment. It is now shadowed by the wrapper on this path only.

surface: nix/generators/base.nix:69-108 (the two shipped example agents, heartbeat.py.timer and sysinfo.py.service); adk/python/agent/runner.py:338 and :422 (the 'unknown' id default); core/agentmgr/discovery.go:164-176 (registry keyed by id, first occurrence wins)
violation: THE IMAGE'S TWO EXAMPLE AGENTS DECLARED NO ID, SO THEY WERE THE SAME AGENT AND ONE OF THEM VANISHED. runner.py derives an agent's id from ID/id/agent_id and falls back to the literal string 'unknown' when none is declared (:338, :422). Both shipped agents omitted it, so both described as 'unknown'; discovery keys its registry by id with first-occurrence-wins and skips a duplicate as 'already found in higher priority path' (discovery.go:167-171). MEASURED on a booted image once GAPI-DIV-077 made the runner reachable: 'registered agent agent_id=unknown' followed by 'agent discovery complete count=1' - two agents in the directory, one registration, under a name that identifies nothing. THESE ARE THE EXAMPLES. They are the only agents most operators will ever see, they are what a first image boot demonstrates, and they modelled an omission that silently costs an agent. The metadata comment already in this file - 'Real module-level assignments, not comments... a commented TYPE = timer is silently dropped' - was written about exactly this class of silent metadata loss and did not extend to the id.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (a shipped example is documentation, and documentation that models a defect teaches it); goblin/gapi identity rules (an agent id names one agent)
exit: RESOLVED 2026-08-04 by declaring ID = "heartbeat" and ID = "sysinfo" in the two agents, with a comment recording why it is not optional. CLOSES ON nix/tests/generator-agents.nix requiring BOTH names in gapictl agent status output - the previous state passed any test that merely counted agents as non-zero, which is why the count assertion in this repository's earlier drafts would not have caught it. VERIFIED: 'registered agent agent_id=heartbeat', 'registered agent agent_id=sysinfo', 'agent discovery complete count=2'. RESIDUAL, and it is the larger half of this finding: THE ADK'S DEFAULT IS THE REAL DEFECT. Falling back to the literal 'unknown' guarantees a collision the moment two agents omit the id, and the collision is silent at every layer - the runner does not warn, and discovery logs the skip at DEBUG. A filename-derived default (heartbeat.py.timer -> heartbeat) would make omission harmless and is what most unit systems do; refusing to describe an agent with no id would make it loud. Either is better than a shared constant. NOT CHANGED HERE because it is an ADK contract change affecting both language SDKs and belongs with GAPI-DIV-062's parity work, not in a nix generator fix.

surface: core/agentmgr/discovery.go:216-222 (the python branch's error handling, comment 'quiet for mixed folders'); :236-243 (the binary branch, same shape); :167-171 (the duplicate skip, logged at DEBUG)
violation: DISCOVERY DISCARDS A FAILED AGENT SILENTLY, AND THAT SILENCE HID THREE SEPARATE DEFECTS IN ONE EVENING. A file whose name matches the agent convention (*.py.service, *.py.timer, *.py.socket) has ALREADY declared itself an agent. If pythonDescribe then fails - no runner, no interpreter, a syntax error, a missing dependency, a bad metadata value - discovery does 'return nil' with the log line commented out, at no level. The daemon then reports 'agent discovery complete count=0' and 'no agents registered in manager' at INFO, which is indistinguishable from an empty directory. The stated justification, 'quiet for mixed folders', describes a real concern about directories holding non-agent files - but that concern is already served by the NAME CHECK above it. Once a file matches *.py.timer, it is not a stray README; it is a broken agent, and the operator is the person who can fix it. MEASURED COST: GAPI-DIV-077 (no runner in the image) presented as count=0 with no diagnostic, and finding it took booting a VM, reading the journal, then reading the discovery source - none of which an operator would do, because nothing indicated anything was wrong. The binary branch at :236-243 has the identical shape ('Not a GAPI agent binary'), where the same argument applies with less force because an executable in a directory really may be unrelated.
rule: go-project-manifesto (errors are data, not strings, and are not discarded at a boundary); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 5 (a gate whose success is indistinguishable from its absence is not a gate - GAPI-DIV-044's finding, applied to discovery rather than to CI)
exit: A file that matched the agent naming convention and then failed to describe MUST produce a log line naming the path and the error. WARN is the right level for the python branch: the name is an explicit declaration of intent, so failing it is a defect in the deployment rather than noise. The binary branch is a genuine judgement call and DEBUG may be correct there, since an unrelated executable is plausible; if so, say that in the comment instead of the current one, which claims a rationale the python branch does not have. CLOSES ON: a test that puts a *.py.timer with deliberately broken metadata in a search path and asserts the log carries its path and a reason - not merely that discovery returned zero agents, which is the assertion that passes today and proves nothing. NOT AN EXIT: raising the count log to WARN when it is zero. That reports a symptom without the cause and would have said nothing about which of the four possible failures was in play. SEQUENCING: independent of everything else; it is the change that would have made GAPI-DIV-077 and -078 self-diagnosing, and it should land before the next agent-loading change rather than after. RESIDUAL ON ARRIVAL: the duplicate-id skip at :167-171 is also DEBUG-level, and that one silently drops a WORKING agent (GAPI-DIV-078). It deserves the same treatment and is arguably worse, since nothing about the surviving agent looks wrong. ||| RESOLVED 2026-08-05. Both branches now report, with the path and the error. THE PYTHON BRANCH IS WARN, as the exit requires: a name matching *.py.<type> is an explicit declaration of intent, so failing to describe it is a defect in the deployment rather than noise, and the comment it replaced ('quiet for mixed folders') named a concern the name check above already serves. THE BINARY BRANCH IS DEBUG and says why in its own comment rather than inheriting the python branch's rationale: an executable on a search path has declared nothing, so it may legitimately be an unrelated program and a warning would be noise an operator cannot act on. It is still reported with path and reason, because the cost of being wrong there is a real agent binary skipped in silence. TESTS. TestDiscovery_ReportsAPythonAgentThatFailedToDescribe puts a syntactically broken *.py.timer in a search path and asserts a WARN carrying its path - asserting on WHAT WAS REPORTED rather than on the returned count, which is the assertion that passes today and proves nothing. TestDiscovery_ReportsAnExecutableThatIsNotAnAgent covers the binary branch and deliberately asserts the LEVEL-INDEPENDENT property, that the skip is reported at all, so a defensible change to the level does not read as a regression. Both use a local log sink rather than adopted_linux_test.go's captureRecords, which is Linux-only while core/agentmgr builds elsewhere - depending on it would have made these tests vanish on any other platform, which is this entry's own defect class. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE: restoring the silent `return nil` fails the python test and only that one. VERIFIED: mage -v test exit 0 (29 packages, zero FAIL), mage -v lint exit 0 with Issues 0. THE RESIDUAL IS DISCHARGED TO GAPI-DIV-091 RATHER THAN CLOSED HERE, and this entry's framing of it was wrong: the duplicate-id skip is not the same defect at a different level. It is a message asserting a cause it never checked, and its two cases - a collision inside one search path versus the designed cross-path shadowing of operator decision 7 - want OPPOSITE treatment. Distinguishing them needs origin tracking, not a log level.

surface: tools.go (the main module's tool anchors); tools/gopy/tools.go and tools/gopy/go.mod (a SEPARATE module, which is why the anchor cannot live there); .gitignore:55 (adk/python/gapi/native/adk.go); Magefile.go Python{}.Build; vendor/github.com/go-python/gopy/gopyh
violation: THE VENDOR TREE CARRIED A PACKAGE THAT `go mod vendor` DELETES, AND THE PYTHON ADK BUILD DEPENDS ON IT. github.com/go-python/gopy/gopyh is the RUNTIME half of gopy: it is imported by adk/python/gapi/native/adk.go, which `gopy gen` writes at build time and which .gitignore:55 excludes from the repository. So NO COMMITTED SOURCE IMPORTS IT, `go mod vendor` correctly prunes it as unreachable from the module graph, and the very next build fails - the generated file is then compiled under -mod=vendor against a vendor tree that no longer contains what it imports. MEASURED, gapi CI run 30966848761, step 'Build Python ADK Bindings': 'adk.go:57:2: cannot find module providing package github.com/go-python/gopy/gopyh: import lookup disabled by -mod=vendor'. THE DEFECT WAS DORMANT FOR AS LONG AS NOBODY RE-VENDORED. gopyh was present in vendor/ on main, so every build worked; it survived only because no `go mod vendor` had run since it was first added. The first re-vendor to follow - the magelib v0.7.0 bump for GAPI-DIV-067's terminology gate - removed it, and a routine dependency bump broke the ADK build. That is the trap shape: a tree that is correct only until someone runs the standard command for maintaining it. THE ANCHOR THAT LOOKED PRESENT WAS THE WRONG ONE. Both tools.go files import github.com/go-python/gopy, the COMMAND, which does not import gopyh - anchoring a tool does not anchor the runtime its generated output needs. AND THE OBVIOUS PLACE TO FIX IT IS WRONG: tools/gopy/tools.go reads like the natural home and is a SEPARATE MODULE with its own go.mod (pinning gopy v0.4.10 deliberately, because that release pins an x/tools that will not compile here), so this module's `go mod vendor` never sees its imports. An anchor added there has no effect at all, which was confirmed by adding one and watching the prune happen again.
rule: go-project-manifesto (a build must be reproducible from the committed tree; a vendor directory that only works until `go mod vendor` runs is not vendored state, it is a fossil); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 5 (a dependency that no declaration reaches is not declared)
exit: RESOLVED 2026-08-04 by anchoring the runtime package explicitly in the MAIN module's tools.go: `_ "github.com/go-python/gopy/gopyh"` alongside the existing command anchors, under the //go:build tools constraint that already guards them. That is the canonical Go answer for a dependency the build needs but no ordinary source imports, and it makes vendoring REPEATABLE rather than one-shot. CLOSES ON `go mod vendor` retaining vendor/github.com/go-python/gopy/gopyh/handle.go, verified directly, and on the step that failed passing: `mage python:build` now reports 'Python bindings built successfully', exit 0, having run gopy gen, goimports, the adk_go.so build and the _adk.so link. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE, and not deliberately - CI produced the failure before the fix existed, which is the strongest form of it. The anchor was also FIRST ADDED TO THE WRONG FILE, and that is worth keeping: tools/gopy/tools.go is a separate module, the prune recurred unchanged, and only moving the import into the root tools.go retained the package. RESIDUAL 1: nothing asserts this stays true. The gate that would catch a recurrence is a CI step that runs `go mod vendor` and fails on a dirty tree, which would also catch every other drift between go.mod and vendor/; it does not exist in any of the three repos. RESIDUAL 2: the same shape can exist for any other package reachable only from generated, gitignored code. gopyh is the only one found, by the failure rather than by a sweep, and no sweep has been done. RESIDUAL 3: the two tools.go files now differ in purpose in a way their names do not convey - the root one anchors what the MODULE needs vendored, the tools/gopy one anchors what a SEPARATE tool module builds. The comment added to the root file records the distinction, because the next person will reach for the wrong one exactly as this fix did.

surface: adk/python/agent/runner.py describe() - the metadata binding near the top of the function and the inspect.getmembers loop that rebinds the same identifier
violation: EVERY PYTHON AGENT REPORTS THE WRONG NAME. describe() binds `name` from the metadata aliases, then the capability scan reuses the identifier as its loop variable - `for name, obj in inspect.getmembers(mod)` - so by the time describe_data is assembled, `name` holds the LAST member inspect.getmembers returned rather than the declared or defaulted value. Demonstrated against test/adk/fixtures/python/lifecycle_agent.py, which declares no NAME and should therefore default to its id: the payload reads {"id": "lifecycle_agent", "name": "stop"}, and `stop` is a lifecycle function on that module. THE BUG SURVIVED BECAUSE NOTHING READS name. It is emitted by both producers, asserted for presence by the cross-ADK key set, and typed in adk/python/gapi/schemas.py - yet no live consumer reads it: core/agentmgr/discovery.go's pyDescribe has no such field, and the only struct that does, core/adk/meta.AgentInfo, is unreachable (GAPI-DIV-082). A field that is produced, asserted for presence, and read by nobody can be wrong indefinitely.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 5 (the parity contract is the SDK's real API); design/adk-architecture.md (every field in the descriptor has a consumer)
exit: describe() stops reusing the identifier - the capability scan binds its own loop variables - and a test asserts the declared name survives capability derivation, with one fixture declaring a NAME distinct from its id and one declaring none, since the defaulted path is what fails today. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE: restore the shadowing and the assertion fails. LAND THIS BEFORE GAPI-DIV-062, and separately. Moving assembly into Go repairs this as a side effect, so folding it into that work would close a live defect without anyone recording that it existed. ||| RESOLVED 2026-08-05. The capability scan no longer binds the member name - `for _, obj in inspect.getmembers(mod)` - because it never used it: the binding was purely a side effect, and the side effect was clobbering the declared name three lines after it was read. THE REGRESSION LIVES IN test/adk RATHER THAN IN THE PYTHON SUITE, and that placement is deliberate: adk/python/tests is executed by nothing (GAPI-DIV-090, filed from this work), so a test there would not have run. TestDescribe_ReportsTheDeclaredName drives the real invocation - python3, the runner, --module, --describe - against a new fixture declaring NAME distinct from ID; TestDescribe_DefaultsNameToID covers the other half against a fixture declaring none. Both failed with name="stop" before the fix, that being the last member inspect.getmembers returned for those modules. THE NEW FIXTURE WAS NECESSARY because no existing Python fixture declares a NAME at all: the reported name defaulted to the id everywhere, so a payload that had lost the declared name still looked plausible. LANDED BEFORE GAPI-DIV-062 AND SEPARATELY, as this entry required - moving describe assembly into Go repairs this as a side effect and would have closed a live defect with nothing recording that it existed.

surface: nix/package.nix postInstall (cp -r adk/python, with no gopy step anywhere in the derivation); Magefile.go:533 (the only generator of adk/python/gapi/native); core/agentmgr/python_agent.go:412

FIRST STEP IS CONFIRMATION, because the entire entry is an inference: build the image, place one *.py.service, start it in production mode, and record what happens. If it fails, that failure is the evidence. If it succeeds, find out what supplied the extension and record THAT, because it is not this derivation. COUPLED TO GAPI-DIV-086 - making discovery strict against a package that never built the binding converts a silent degradation into a visible failure, which is the intent, but the two want landing together. ||| CONFIRMED 2026-08-05, AND THE ENTRY'S COST IS UNDERSTATED. The inference is now an observation, and it needed no image: `nix build .#default` produces a store path whose share/gapi/python carries agent/runner.py, the gapi package (agent.py, __init__.py, protocols.py, schemas.py) and even tests/, with NO gapi/native directory and NO .so anywhere beneath it. Invoked as DISCOVERY invokes it, with no ADK_REJECT_DUMMY: exit 0, a full describe payload on stdout, and '[WARNING] Running with DummyAdk (stdout fallback mode)' on stderr. Invoked as a PRODUCTION-MODE START invokes it, with ADK_REJECT_DUMMY=1: exit 1, zero bytes of stdout, and '[FATAL] Failed to import gapi.native.adk and ADK_REJECT_DUMMY is set: No module named gapi.native'. surface: adk/go/core.go:94 SendEvent; adk/go/core.go:172 StartHeartbeat and the fmt.Sprintf at :177; core/agentmgr/go_agent.go:599-613 (the stdout control reader)
violation: AN AGENT'S EVENT IS SERIALIZED, IMMEDIATELY DESERIALIZED, AND RE-SERIALIZED BEFORE IT LEAVES THE PROCESS. SendEvent takes a JSON STRING, json.Unmarshals it into map[string]interface{}, plucks event/id/state/run_id by key, builds a LifecycleStatus, wraps it in Any and publishes over QUIC. The wire is ALREADY protobuf; the JSON is a hand-parsed intermediate between the agent and its own ADK, and it buys nothing. THREE CONSEQUENCES, all visible in those two functions. (1) StartHeartbeat builds its JSON with fmt.Sprintf and NO ESCAPING (core.go:177), so an agent id containing a quote emits malformed JSON every five seconds. (2) The event name is extracted and then discarded - `_ = event // Topic logic uses fixed string for now` - so every event publishes to one hardcoded topic and every subscriber filters what it should have selected. (3) `Message: jsonStr` stuffs the whole blob into a text field, so the structure survives only as text. THE STDOUT PATH IS THE SAME PROBLEM FROM THE OTHER END: with no QUIC client SendEvent prints the JSON, and go_agent.go:599 scans the child's stdout line by line, unmarshalling each line and treating anything unparseable as a log line - so one stream carries both a protocol and arbitrary program output, and which one a line IS depends on whether it happens to parse.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 5 (protobuf for inter-process communication); design/adk-architecture.md (agents do not construct wire formats; the topic derives from the event's type; stdout carries logs only)
exit: Agents report events by calling a typed ADK function, and the ADK publishes the protobuf it was given with the topic derived from the event type. Python builds a generated message and passes it across the binding. For a running agent stdout carries log lines only; --describe stays a separate invocation that emits one descriptor and exits. Events produced before the transport is up are buffered and flushed on connect, with overflow dropped, COUNTED and reported - a dropped event nothing records is indistinguishable from one that never happened. CLOSES ON: no JSON string on any event-producing path, plus a test that an agent id containing a quote produces a well-formed heartbeat, which fails today. INDEPENDENT of the descriptor work; the two share only the binding surface.

AwaitCommand blocks on a condition variable until cmdMailbox.cmd is non-empty; the only thing that ever sets it is InjectCommand, described in its own comment as 'a helper for testing/simulation'. Neither is called anywhere in gapi or goblin - not in production code, and not in tests. AwaitCommand's own comment says the quiet part: 'In a real implementation, this would read from a QUIC stream or IPC socket.' THIS COSTS MORE THAN DEAD CODE USUALLY DOES. gopy binds every exported symbol in adk/go into the native extension, which is why that package's exported surface is a deliberate constraint and why the Go agent runtime lives in adk/go/agent instead. Two slots of that constrained surface are spent on a mechanism that does nothing, and because they are Python-visible an agent author can call AwaitCommand and block forever.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (a mechanism nothing drives is not a mechanism); design/adk-architecture.md (a symbol exported and never called is a permanent part of a constrained surface)
exit: Delete both, and the mailbox with them. If a supervisor-to-agent command channel is wanted it should be designed rather than inherited: it is the inverse of the event channel in GAPI-DIV-087, belongs on the same transport, and should carry the same schema. What must not happen is the stub surviving into the new binding surface because it was already there. CLOSES ON: adk/go's exported symbol count DROPS, and the cross-ADK suite still passes. ||| RESOLVED 2026-08-05. AwaitCommand, InjectCommand and the cmdMailbox they shared are deleted, along with the init that built its condition variable. THE GATE THIS ENTRY NAMED IS MET AND MEASURABLE: adk/go's exported surface drops from TEN symbols to EIGHT - StartQUIC, Initialize, SetSchemaHash, ComputeSchemaHash, SendEvent, StartHeartbeat, ChannelManager and NewChannelManager remain, every one of them a mechanism the ADK owns on the agent's behalf. THE GENERATED BINDING PROVED THE COUPLING: after the deletion the build failed in adk/python/gapi/native/adk.go with `undefined: adk.AwaitCommand` and `undefined: adk.InjectCommand` at three call sites, because gopy had generated wrappers for both. Regenerating with `mage -v python:build` cleared it, which is the same fact the entry was making: every exported symbol here becomes Python-visible surface whether or not anything drives it. A comment records what was removed and why, and states the constructive half - a command channel is the inverse of SendEvent's path and belongs on the same transport carrying the same schema (GAPI-DIV-087), so it should be designed rather than restored from this stub. VERIFIED: build and vet clean, python:build regenerates and links _adk.so, mage -v test and mage -v lint green.

surface: core/agentmgr/python_agent.go (813 lines); core/agentmgr/go_agent.go (745 lines)

The control-stream reader, the environment assembly and the describe surface are three candidates, and the first two are where the two files duplicate one another, so extracting them shortens both at once. surface: adk/python/tests/test_runner.py; .github/workflows/ci.yml:57,119 (mage python:build, the only Python step in CI); Magefile.go's Python namespace
violation: THE PYTHON ADK'S TEST SUITE IS NEVER RUN. adk/python/tests/test_runner.py exists and exercises runner.py's capability extraction directly, and nothing invokes it: no mage target runs unittest or pytest, and CI's only Python step is `mage -v python:build`, which is gopy generation plus build.py. The suite is therefore indistinguishable from an absent one - it can rot, fail, or assert the wrong thing indefinitely with no signal anywhere. FOUND WHILE FIXING GAPI-DIV-081. That regression's natural home was this suite, and putting it there would have produced a test that never ran; it went into test/adk instead, driven from Go, because that is the only place a Python-behaviour assertion is currently executed. THAT IS A WORKAROUND RATHER THAN A DESIGN: asserting Python behaviour through a Go subprocess test costs a process spawn per case, and it can only reach what is observable on stdout - the capability-extraction logic the existing suite tests directly is not reachable that way at all.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 5 (a gate whose success is indistinguishable from its absence is not a gate - GAPI-DIV-044's finding, applied to the Python suite); python-project-manifesto

A red first run is the entry doing its job, not a reason to abandon the change. CLOSES ON: a deliberately broken assertion in adk/python/tests failing CI, which is the only way to tell this apart from the state it is in now.

surface: core/agentmgr/discovery.go:167-170 (the duplicate-id skip and the message it emits)
violation: THE DUPLICATE-ID SKIP ASSERTS A RATIONALE IT NEVER CHECKED. When two agents describe with the same id, discovery keeps the first and logs 'skipping agent already found in higher priority path' at DEBUG. That sentence is true only when the collision spans search paths. GAPI-DIV-078's actual case was two agents IN ONE DIRECTORY, both defaulting to the id 'unknown' because neither declared one - there was no higher-priority path, and the line said there was. THE TWO CASES WANT OPPOSITE TREATMENT. A collision WITHIN one search path is a defect: two agents were installed and one silently does not exist. A collision ACROSS search paths is the designed precedence - operator decision 7, configuration beats runtime beats data beats vendor - which exists so an operator can override a vendored agent, and warning on it would fire on every layered deployment doing exactly what it was told. DISCOVERY CANNOT TELL THEM APART TODAY: `discovered` is keyed by id across all paths and the loop records nothing about which path registered an id, so the message picks one explanation and states it unconditionally. FILED SEPARATELY FROM GAPI-DIV-079, whose residual named this: that entry was about SILENCE and this one is about a CLAIM, and closing it needs origin tracking rather than a log level.
rule: go-project-manifesto (errors are data, not strings - a diagnostic asserting an unchecked cause misleads more than silence); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (a message an operator is expected to act on must be true)
exit: Discovery records which search path registered each id, and the skip distinguishes the two cases: a collision inside one path reports a defect at WARN naming BOTH files, and a collision across paths reports shadowing - DEBUG or INFO, being designed behaviour - naming the winner and the loser. Neither message may claim a precedence relationship it did not check. CLOSES ON: two tests, one per case, asserting the messages differ. A single test proves nothing here, because today's line passes the cross-path case by accident. NOTE WHAT IS ALREADY DONE: GAPI-DIV-079 made the failure-to-describe branches report, so an agent that fails to LOAD is now visible. This entry covers only the agent that loads correctly and is then discarded, which is the harder one to notice because nothing about the surviving agent looks wrong.

surface: pkg/cli/agent_go_source.go buildGoAgent:413 (the staging directory), :442 (go build with build.Dir = stage), :324 (adkImportPath), and the KNOWN LIMIT comment at :404-411 that already states this
violation: A GO AGENT CANNOT BE BUILT BY ANYONE WHO INSTALLED GAPI RATHER THAN CLONED IT. `gapictl agent build` stages the assembled package in a temp directory beside the author's source and runs `go build .` there. Outside a Go module that fails immediately: `go: go.mod file not found in current directory or any parent directory`, and the command exits 1. MEASURED against the packaged binaries in a clean directory: `gapictl agent new --lang=go --type=service demo` writes src/agents/demo.go.service and prints 'Next steps: 2. Build: gapictl agent build src/agents/demo.go.service'. That command - the tool's own instruction - cannot succeed. THE LIMIT IS KNOWN AND WAS NEVER FILED. buildGoAgent's comment says it plainly: 'KNOWN LIMIT, recorded rather than hidden: this therefore assumes the agent lives inside a checkout that can resolve the kernel. A standalone gapictl building an agent in an unrelated directory needs a generated go.mod, which this does not do.' A comment in a function body is not the ledger, and nothing else records it - a search of every entry for go.mod, standalone or agent build returns only resolved entries mentioning them incidentally. THE STAGING CHOICE IS DELIBERATE AND CORRECT FOR THE CASE IT SERVES: staging beside the author's file keeps the assembled package inside whatever module the agent already lives in, so the ADK import resolves without reaching the module proxy. The defect is not that choice; it is that the standalone case has no path at all, while the CLI advertises one. THIS IS THE PRODUCT'S HEADLINE CAPABILITY. Go is the language the ecosystem is written in, and the Go agent is the form the architecture treats as canonical - 'a single file, not a program'. Every other open entry in this area concerns a diagnostic, a schema or a dead symbol; this one decides whether the feature exists for an operator.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (a capability the tool advertises and cannot perform is not a capability); design/adk-architecture.md (gapictl agent build assembles the author's file and a generated main, and the author writes no flags)
exit: `gapictl agent build` succeeds against a source file in a directory that is not a Go module, producing a binary that describes and runs. THREE ROUTES, and the choice is a real design decision rather than an implementation detail. (1) GENERATE A go.mod IN THE STAGE with a require on the kernel at the version gapictl was built from - simplest, but it reaches the module proxy, so an offline or air-gapped host still cannot build. (2) SHIP THE ADK SOURCE IN THE PACKAGE and generate a go.mod with a `replace` pointing at it: the derivation already installs share/gapi/python, so share/gapi/go is the same move, and it keeps the build offline. (3) DECLARE THE STANDALONE CASE UNSUPPORTED and make the CLI say so instead of printing a command that fails - the cheapest honest option, and it makes GAPI-DIV-093 mostly moot. PROVENANCE CONSTRAINT, which routes 1 and 2 must not walk past: buildGoAgent hashes the staged package with crypto.HashDirectory(stage, "*.go") at :427 and stamps it via -ldflags SourceHash. A generated go.mod determines WHICH ADK version is compiled in and would not be covered by that hash, so adding one without extending the hash silently weakens the provenance the stamp claims. CLOSES ON: a test that builds an agent from a directory outside any module and runs --describe on the result. Note it must create that directory OUTSIDE the repo tree, since a test running under the gapi checkout inherits its go.mod and would pass while proving nothing. ||| RESOLVED 2026-08-05. ROUTE 2 was taken, on an operator decision, and taken FURTHER than this entry described: the stage is self-contained ALWAYS, in the checkout as well as the install, so there is one build path rather than two. WHAT MADE ROUTE 2 CHEAP WAS A FACT THIS ENTRY DID NOT CARRY. adk/go/agent is STDLIB-ONLY - `go list -deps ./adk/go/agent` returns 79 packages of which exactly one is not stdlib, itself - and it is 734 hand-written lines in five files. Shipping it is five files and a generated go.mod, no vendor tree and no third-party anything. That is only true of adk/go/AGENT: adk/go, the gopy backend, imports core/eventbus, core/transport, pkg/proto and two internal packages, and could not be shipped this way. The separation the architecture made for gopy's sake is exactly the cut this needed. Nothing in the daemon or the CLI compiles it either - `go list -deps ./cmd/...` contains no adk package, and the only in-module references are two tests and adkImportPath, which is a STRING CONSTANT and not an import. HOW IT WORKS. resolveGoADK (pkg/cli/agent_go_adk.go) locates the ADK through three tiers in the same order and for the same reasons as resolvePyRunner - <PREFIX>_GO_ADK, then the install tree at <prefix>/share/<product>/go, then the checkout - differing in TWO ways, both deliberate. The last tier is CHECKED rather than returned on faith, so a missing tree produces a message naming the ADK instead of a go build failure about modules. And it WALKS UP from the working directory rather than trusting that directory to be the repository root. THE SECOND DIFFERENCE WAS LEARNED FROM A RED CI RUN, not designed in: the tier was first written as a bare 'adk/go' relative to the cwd, copying resolvePyRunner's SHAPE and its weakness together, and every Go case in the cross-language parity suite failed with 'cannot locate the Go ADK source' because the harness runs gapictl from test/adk. That is GAPI-DIV-077's third tier exactly - a cwd-relative path that happens to hit in a dev tree and resolves against / on a booted system. TestResolveGoADKFindsTheCheckoutFromASubdirectory is the gate; it earns its keep by living in pkg/cli, two levels down, so a resolver that only checks the working directory fails it. THE CAUSE IS ONE LINE. quic.go:258 returns io.ErrUnexpectedEOF when no peer connection exists. That sentinel means 'a read ended before it should have'; here it is being used to mean 'there is nobody to send to', which is not an error at all on a node with no peers. The bus cannot tell the two apart, so eventbus.go:417 logs every occurrence at ERROR. ERRORS AS STRINGS RATHER THAN DATA, and the cost is the usual one: a genuine transport failure on a real cluster produces exactly the same line as a single node behaving perfectly, so the message cannot be alerted on, cannot be grepped for, and trains an operator to ignore the level. IT ALSO DROWNS EVERYTHING ELSE. Better than a third of a fresh daemon's output is this line, which is the first thing anyone reads when diagnosing something unrelated - GAPI-DIV-077 and -078 were both found by reading exactly this log.
rule: go-project-manifesto (errors are data, not strings); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (a diagnostic that fires during correct operation is not a diagnostic)
exit: Publishing to zero peers is not a failure. Either PublishRemote returns nil when no connection exists - the honest reading, since the event has nowhere to go and nothing went wrong - or it returns a TYPED sentinel (ErrNoPeer) that the bus recognises and does not log at ERROR. The typed form is preferable: it keeps the distinction available to a caller that does care, which a bare nil discards. DO NOT FIX THIS BY LOWERING THE LEVEL AT THE BUS: that hides real transport failures behind the same treatment and inverts the defect rather than removing it. CLOSES ON: a single-node daemon start producing ZERO transport-publish errors across a full agent lifecycle, plus a test that a genuine publish failure - a connection that exists and then breaks - still logs at ERROR. One assertion without the other is how this gets 'fixed' into silence. ||| RESOLVED 2026-08-05. eventbus.ErrNoPeer is the typed sentinel. surface: Magefile.go Python{}.Build, the gcc link step (the -Wl,-rpath,$ORIGIN flag and the exec.Command("sh", "-c", ...) that ran it); adk/python/gapi/native/adk.py:14-20 (gopy's generated chdir shim, which masked the defect)

The manifesto names three invariants of the binding build - `go build -mod=mod`, the `-Wl,-rpath,$ORIGIN` link flag, and the generate-then-goimports ordering - and says each 'lives in the binding build task with a comment stating what breaks without it'. The flag was there. The linker never received it. Python{}.Build composed the whole gcc command line into ONE STRING and ran it with exec.Command("sh", "-c", cmd), so the shell expanded $ORIGIN as an UNDEFINED VARIABLE to the empty string and gcc got `-Wl,-rpath,` - an EMPTY rpath entry. MEASURED on the extension this repo builds today: `patchelf --print-rpath _adk.so` returns `:/home/.../gapi/outputs/out/lib:/nix/store/python3.../lib:...` - note the leading colon, which IS the empty entry, and note that the second path does not exist on disk. No $ORIGIN anywhere. The surrounding comment says 'we need to ensure RPATH is there', which is how long this has read as done. IT WORKED ANYWAY, FOR A REASON THIS REPO DOES NOT CONTROL. _adk.so links adk_go.so by BARE SONAME, so the loader must find it beside the extension. What actually satisfies that is gopy's GENERATED adk.py, which chdirs the whole process into the native directory around `from . import _adk` and chdirs back (adk.py:14-20); glibc resolves the empty rpath entry as the current directory, which is then the native dir. So the mechanism keeping the Python ADK importable is an undocumented side effect of generated code, reinstated on every regeneration, and it also means importing the ADK MUTATES PROCESS-GLOBAL STATE - a cwd change any concurrent thread sees. THE COST IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND IT LANDS ON GAPI-DIV-085. Nix's fixupPhase runs patchelf --shrink-rpath, which drops non-existent and empty entries and PRESERVES $ORIGIN. DEMONSTRATED END TO END on a copy of adk/python with the current extension: after shrink-rpath, `import gapi.native.adk` from outside the tree fails with `ImportError: adk_go.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`; relinking the same tree's extension with a literal $ORIGIN makes the same import succeed. So the packaging step -085 exists to add would have produced an extension that cannot load, and the failure would have named a missing .so rather than a link flag.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (the binding build's invariants are pinned in the build, not in memory; each lives in the build task with a comment stating what breaks without it); go-project-manifesto (explicit over clever - a command assembled into a string and handed to a shell is reinterpreted by that shell)
exit: The linked extension carries $ORIGIN, and the build proves it rather than the command implying it. FIX THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE: quoting the flag would work and leaves the next argument exposed to the same expansion, so the link step splits python3-config's flags in Go and execs gcc directly, with no shell between the arguments and the linker. CLOSES ON: Python{}.Build reading the linked _adk.so's ELF dynamic section and FAILING when neither DT_RUNPATH nor DT_RPATH contains $ORIGIN. That is the gate, and it must read the ARTIFACT - this entry exists precisely because the command was correct and the output was not. Use debug/elf from the standard library rather than shelling out to patchelf or readelf: a gate needing a tool the build does not already require is a gate that gets skipped on the machine where it matters. NOTE FOR GAPI-DIV-085: this is a prerequisite, not a consequence. Packaging the extension without it produces an artifact that imports in the source tree and fails in the store path, which is the same shape as -085 itself and would have been diagnosed as a Python problem. ||| RESOLVED 2026-08-05, in the change that found it. The link step no longer builds a command string: it splits python3-config's cflags and ldflags in Go and execs gcc directly, so nothing between the argument list and the linker can reinterpret an argument. `-Wl,-rpath,$ORIGIN` now reaches gcc literally, and `patchelf --print-rpath _adk.so` returns `$ORIGIN:...` with $ORIGIN FIRST. THE GATE IS assertOriginRunpath, called by Python{}.Build immediately after the link. It opens the produced _adk.so with debug/elf and fails unless DT_RUNPATH or DT_RPATH contains a $ORIGIN element - the ARTIFACT, not the command, which is the whole lesson of this entry. Standard library, so it adds no tool the build did not already need. PROVEN BY REVERSION: changing the flag back to an empty rpath makes the build fail with `_adk.so carries no $ORIGIN run path (found [":/home/.../outputs/out/lib:..."])`, the leading colon visible in the reported value, and Magefile.go was restored sha256-identical. WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: after Nix's fixupPhase the extension keeps $ORIGIN and loses only the entries that never existed, so GAPI-DIV-085 can package it. The gopy chdir shim in the generated adk.py is untouched and still runs - it is generated code this repo does not own - but it is no longer the only thing making the import work.
